text:
maria: ran the sampling vs eager-evict experiment on the paged-attn workload (30k live kv entries, mixed short/long seqs). saw a weird bimodal OOM pattern when we hit compaction. attaching quick numbers and a trace id

maria: experiment summary (30m run, p95 latency, memory spike, compaction time)
```
> sampling-compaction: p95=86ms, mem-spike=8.1GB, compaction-cost=420ms, kv-hit=0.72
> eager-evict:        p95=94ms, mem-spike=6.2GB, compaction-cost=120ms, kv-hit=0.65
> baseline (no compaction): p95=78ms, mem-spike=9.8GB, compaction-cost=0, kv-hit=0.74
```

maria: interestingly sampling has better latency but occasionally triggers long compactions that cause OOM fallback on small-device runs. trace id: trace-7751

raj: can you paste the nsight slice or flamegraph? curious which kernel is blocking during compaction window

maria: pasted relevant nsys slice (brief):
```
nsys export --trace=trace-7751 --range 00:12:18-00:12:20 
# main wait is kernel: block_compact_work (0.36s) + cudaMemcpy (0.04s) + allocator_scan (0.05s)
```

anya: looks like allocator_scan is serializing large free lists. two quick ideas: 1) increase workspace_target to avoid large live fragmentation; 2) make compaction chunked (cap per-frame compaction to 128MB) so we don't stall kernels for >200ms

lucas: another angle: the batcher jitter causes short bursts that change kernel selection (we fallback to larger kernel variant during big seqs). if we smooth batcher window by 15ms the compaction events align less with heavy kernels

raj: do we have KV cache hit distribution across block sizes? maybe sampling is keeping many small blocks alive and compaction cost becomes superlinear

maria: good point. here's a quick histogram from the run (block_size_bytes -> live_count):
```
16KB -> 8.9k
32KB -> 3.1k
64KB -> 420
128KB -> 90
256KB -> 11
```

maria: sampling kept many 16KB/32KB fragments which keeps compaction scanning hot. eager-evict reduces live small fragments but increases churn (lower kv-hit). tradeoff is between compaction latency vs hit-rate

anya: subtlety: compaction-cost is not pure mem-copy; kernel selection also changes because workspace sizing influences which attention kernel path we pick. If compaction reduces workspace just before a long seq arrival we force fallback to slower kernel -> multimodal p95

lucas: small experiment proposal: 1) run chunked compaction limit=128MB + workspace_min_pct=20 2) smoother batcher (jitter=15ms) 3) allocator: fast-free threshold=64KB (coalesce small frees asynchronously) 4) measure p95, mem-spike, kv-hit

maria: queued the job on staging with those flags, run id: run-4823. infra-bot: can you attach the job link? @infra-bot

infra-bot: deployed job run-4823 to staging (gpu-pool-small). logs: https://ci.internal/runs/run-4823 :rocket:

raj: nice. if that stabilizes p95 without increasing mem-spike we can try graduating to dedicated and run longer load tests. also capture kernel-selection histogram (which kernel chosen per sequence length)

maria: agreed. I'll collect nsys + allocator traces. will post a short summary after the 2h run. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

lucas: tiny note — if we go with async coalesce make sure to bound CPU work; we saw spikes in the past when coalesce jobs piled up on the main reactor thread

anya: acknowledged. async coalesce will be on a separate worker pool with backpressure

maria: ok closing loop here, will update when run finishes (last_message trace-7751 + run-4823).
